intro: Eight credible frameworks for building LLM agents in 2025–2026. They sit at different points on the control / determinism / observability axes. The right one is the one whose primitives match your task; the wrong one fights you on every step.

items.title: Claude Agent SDK (Anthropic)
items.whenToUse: Building on Claude. Want the closest match to Anthropic's own agent design (Claude Code, Computer Use, MCP first-class).
items.mechanism: TS/Python SDK. Agent loop primitive + MCP + Skills + computer-use built in. Hooks for permissions, logging, sub-agents.
items.tradeoff: Vendor-coupled to Anthropic. Lowest impedance match for Claude-specific features. Young; surface area still moving.

items.title: LangGraph (LangChain)
items.whenToUse: Stateful, graph-shaped agents with explicit control flow. Production deployments needing time-travel debugging.
items.mechanism: Define nodes + edges. State is persistent. Built-in checkpointing, retry, human-in-the-loop.
items.tradeoff: More verbose than loop-style frameworks. Pays back when you need replayable state machines. Heavyweight ecosystem (LangChain) is opt-in.

items.title: OpenAI Agents SDK
items.whenToUse: Building on OpenAI models. Multi-agent handoffs as first-class primitive.
items.mechanism: Agents define instructions + tools + handoffs. Runner orchestrates. Tracing built in.
items.tradeoff: Tightly coupled to OpenAI. Clean API; smaller feature surface than LangGraph.

items.title: AutoGen (Microsoft)
items.whenToUse: Multi-agent conversational systems. Research-style exploration of agent-to-agent dynamics.
items.mechanism: Conversable agents talk to each other. Group chat, manager agent, code execution.
items.tradeoff: Excellent for prototyping novel topologies. Less polished for production observability.

items.title: CrewAI
items.whenToUse: Role-based agent crews (researcher + writer + critic). Quick to scaffold.
items.mechanism: Define agents with roles + goals + tools. Tasks delegated by role. Sequential or hierarchical processes.
items.tradeoff: Opinionated about the 'crew' metaphor. Great for that shape, awkward outside it.

items.title: smolagents (HuggingFace)
items.mechanism: Agent writes Python code each step instead of structured tool calls. Code is the action space.
items.tradeoff: Very expressive; very dangerous without sandboxing. Best when paired with E2B or similar.

items.title: Pydantic AI
items.whenToUse: Type-safe agents in Python. Structured-output-first design.
items.mechanism: Agents return Pydantic-validated outputs. Dependencies injected for typed tool args. Streaming built in.
items.tradeoff: Best-in-class type safety. Python-only. Less multi-agent affordance than LangGraph/AutoGen.

items.title: Mastra
items.whenToUse: TypeScript-first stack with workflows, evals, RAG, and observability bundled.
items.mechanism: Workflow DSL + agent primitives + dev playground. Designed for serverless + edge.
items.tradeoff: Younger than LangGraph but TS-native. Good when team's existing stack is Node/Next.js.

pitfalls.title: Picking a framework before knowing the task shape
pitfalls.body: Sit down with the task; sketch the graph. THEN pick the framework whose primitives match. Picking framework-first guarantees you'll fight it later.

pitfalls.title: Abstraction tax
pitfalls.body: Every framework adds layers. For a 50-line agent, raw Anthropic SDK is clearer. For a 5000-line stateful workflow, the framework saves you. Match weight to weight.

pitfalls.title: Vendor lock-in via primitives
pitfalls.body: Some frameworks couple tightly to one model family. If you might switch, prefer ones with model-agnostic abstractions.

pitfalls.title: Observability as afterthought
pitfalls.body: Frameworks vary wildly in what they let you see at runtime. Pick one where tracing is first-class; bolting it on is painful.

pitfalls.title: Switching every quarter
pitfalls.body: The field churns fast. Stability of YOUR team's velocity > stability of YOUR choice of framework. Pick one, get good at it, switch only when the cost-of-stay clearly exceeds cost-of-switch.

artifact.content:
<!-- Decision questions. Answer all six before picking. -->

1. Which model provider? Single (locked-in OK) or multi (need agnostic abstractions)?
2. What language is the existing codebase in? Python, TypeScript, or polyglot?
3. What's the agent's expected horizon — single-shot, conversation, or hours-long workflow?
4. Do you need replayable state / checkpoints / time-travel debugging?
5. Do you need first-class multi-agent topology, or single-agent-with-tools?
6. How much will you need to customize the loop vs. accept defaults?

Mapping (rough guidance, not gospel):
- Single-shot Claude + TS → Claude Agent SDK or Mastra.
- Single-shot OpenAI + TS → OpenAI Agents SDK.
- Long-horizon stateful workflow + Python → LangGraph.
- Multi-agent research / topology exploration → AutoGen.
- Role-based crews → CrewAI.
- Code-as-action (sandboxed) → smolagents.
- Type-safe structured outputs + Python → Pydantic AI.
